claim: the auth surface: sign-in, sign-out, account switching, password reset and the throwaway-account cleanup that proves none of it leaked

checks.name: a wrong password does not sign you in
the rejection tells the user what happened
forgot-password answers identically for a real and a fake address
forgot-password does not confirm that an account exists
a bad verification link is refused with a usable message
a rate limit is reported as a rate limit, not as a bad address
a client user can sign in at /login
the employee portal refuses a non-internal account
that refusal did NOT sign the client out of their real portal
an internal user gets through the employee portal
signed in with the current password
the settings page rendered
SECURITY: change-password asks for the CURRENT password
the change-password form rendered
a password change with a WRONG current password is refused
...and the new password really did NOT take effect
...and the real password still works
a password change with the CORRECT current password succeeds
the NEW password works for sign-in
the change can be undone from the UI
the ORIGINAL password works again after the restore
a second session was established for the logout check
the account menu is reachable
there is a 'sign out everywhere' control for a compromised session
Sign out from the account menu ends THIS browser's session
a normal sign-out leaves the other device signed in (local scope)
'sign out everywhere' really does revoke the other device
a signed-in user with no membership lands on the access-denied page
the access-denied page offers 'Sign out & switch account'
'Sign out & switch account' signs the user out and lands on /login
no uncaught page errors during the auth run
no throwaway auth account leaked
no membership rows leaked
no notification rows leaked
no auth users leaked

notes: both paths return the same wording when a send succeeds; the difference here is the environment's mail budget, not the copy
